name: Yakushima
blurb: Ancient cedars, macaques and deer, and turtles nesting in the rain.

tip.title: Remove the loggerheads
tip.text: Set Loggerhead sea turtle to -100% and watch the ripple: jellyfish are no longer eaten, while raccoon dogs, crows, ghost crabs and tiger sharks lose a food source.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Yakushima is among the wettest places in Japan, with several thousand millimetres of rain a year, which keeps the mountain forest constantly damp.
Light drives forest growth and the plankton of the surrounding sea.
Thin, wet forest soil holds the nutrients that the cedars, shrubs and ferns draw on.
Break down fallen wood, leaves, droppings and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil and sea.
Flowering shrubs, with several endemic species on the island, that grow on the high slopes and ridges.

nodes.name: Mosses and liverworts
nodes.desc: The island has many rare mosses and liverworts that carpet trunks, rocks and the forest floor in the damp air.
Microscopic drifting algae at the base of the food web of the sea around the island.

nodes.name: Yakushika (sika deer)
nodes.desc: The island's sika deer is its own subspecies, along with the macaque one of the island's only native large animals. It browses the forest floor.
Drifting animals that graze phytoplankton and feed jellyfish and many other sea animals.
A bold omnivore that scavenges carrion and, like other crows, takes sea turtle eggs and hatchlings.
Beach crabs that scavenge and hunt on sand and prey on turtle eggs and hatchlings.
A big shark that often eats adult sea turtles, which it is well equipped to bite through.
